findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password check
findings.body: In `authorize`, password is only verified when `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`. The new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` is taken even when a dummy `totpCode` is also supplied. An attacker who knows only the victim email and one static backup code can send `password=wrong, totpCode=anything-truthy, backupCode=valid` — the password check is skipped because `totpCode` is truthy, the backup code validates, and login succeeds. This turns a second-factor backup code into a password replacement and defeats the first factor.

findings.title: Backup code matching is fragile and type-unsafe
findings.body: The code does `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` and `indexOf` with no trimming, case normalization, or type check. A correct code pasted with trailing newline/space (e.g. from the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt` file) or typed in uppercase will not match the lowercase hex stored from `setup.ts` and login fails. If `backupCode` is a non-string (array/object from a crafted request) `replaceAll` throws a TypeError, producing a 500 instead of an IncorrectBackupCode 400. Same pattern exists in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`.
